full_judgment:
Naimuddin Ahmed, J: This revisional application is directed against the judgment and order passed by the District Judge, Jamalpur, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 1984 on 16.9.85 whereby he affirmed the judgment and order passed by the Subordinate Judge, Sherpur, in Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 1982 whereby he dismissed the application under Rule 13 of Order 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree in Other Class Suit No. 33 of 1978 disposed of by him on 28.12.1983. 

 2. The facts are that the opposite parties instituted Other Class Suit No. 33 of 1978 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Sherpur and in this suit the present petitioner was the defendant. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 5.5.79 in absence of the petitioner. She then tiled an application under Rule 13 of Order 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground that no summons was served on her and she came to know about the exparte decree on 30.5.82 and this application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 1982. The opposite parties resisted the Miscellaneous case contending that the summons was duly served on the petitioner and that the application was barred by limitation as she had failed to apply for setting aside the ex-parte decree within 30 days after passing of the decree. 

 3. The learned Subordinate Judge found that the summons on the petitioner was duly served and that the application was barred by limitation and as such, he dismissed the miscellaneous case by his judgment and order dated 28.12.83. 

 4. The petitioner than preferred an appeal against the judgment and order before the District Judge, Jamalpur and this appeal was registered as Miscellaneous Appeal No. 8 of 1984. 

 (3) Where service is substituted by order of the Court, the Court shall fix such time for the appearance of the defendant as the case may require." 

 13. it appears from the report of the serving peon in the case before us that the above mandatory requirements of law were not at all complied with, and neither the order of the court nor the report of the serving peon anywhere shows that the summons was affixed at any conspicuous part of the house of the defendant or at the court house. In the above circumstances, it must be held that the courts below failed to appreciate the position of law and apply the law properly on the facts revealed in the case before them. 

 20. The judgment and order of the courts below are hereby set aside and the original Miscellaneous case being Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 1982 of the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Sherpur, is allowed and the ex parte decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 33 of 1978 on 5.5.79 is set aside and the said suit is restored to its file and number. 

 21. In the circumstances of the case the parties are directed to bear their respective costs.
